editorial:
Imagine a world where ancient Greek myths meet Japanese style. You get to watch a story about Medea, a powerful woman who feels totally betrayed by her husband, Jason. He leaves her and their kids to marry a princess just to get more power. You will feel the heat and the anger as Medea plans her revenge. The vibe is very intense and looks like a stage play, but it feels huge because it was filmed in a massive outdoor theater in Athens. It is not your typical movie, but the energy is high and the costumes are stunning.

What really hits home is the acting. The lead actress does an amazing job showing how grief turns into pure rage. Some parts might feel slow since it is based on a play, but the bold colors and loud emotions keep you interested. If you like dramas that don't hold back, you need to see this. You should try to find it on a 4K Blu-ray to add to your collection so you can see all the detail in the sets, or check if you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: In the end, Medea takes her revenge to the furthest limit. To hurt Jason as much as possible, she kills their own children. She does not want Jason to have any family left. After the act, she does not get caught. Instead, she flies away in a golden chariot sent by her grandfather, a sun god. Jason is left alone and broken, losing everything he ever cared about while Medea escapes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about revenge and high-end stage plays.
